Experiment : Structured software development process using composable reusable skills.
Software Development Process : Defining requirements through a clear problem statement and acceptance criteria, then creating a design document aligned with those requirements, my chosen tooling, and current best practices.
Tech Debt Remediation: I also wanted to remediate technical debt by adopting standalone components, modernizing control-flow syntax, converting inputs to signals, using output() and stable signal forms, and replacing appropriate RxJS patterns with resource() or httpResource()
Although these changes can be performed through separate ng generate migration commands, I wanted a more frictionless approach.
This led me to explore spec-driven, or spec-anchored, development — where a specification defines the intended outcomes, scope, non-goals, constraints, acceptance criteria, and deliverables.
I came across the Lattice plugin, which appeared to provide the structured methodology and end-to-end orchestration I needed without requiring me to manually guide every step.
This experiment is to evaluate whether Lattice will meet my need to do the migration.
Approach:
Step 1: Install the Lattice Plugin
codex plugin marketplace add techygarg/latticecodex plugin add lattice@latticeStep 2: Install the Official Angular Skills for Best Practices.

Summary-

• The entire migration took approximately one hour.

• The experiment achieved its intended outcome: migrating the application without manual code changes.

• I reviewed and approved the outcome at each stage before allowing the process to continue.

• I used my personal Codex environment to explore and learn this process independently, with the goal of improving my skills.
